title: customer-portal definition inputs
description: The closed input set of the customer-portal capability: an installation's own developer portal, released from the fleet's backstage bases into extras/backstage of its management-clusters repository, signing people in on the installation's Dex. The renderer turns these inputs into the portal's fileset — the two kustomizations (without apiVersion and kind, as the fleet writes them, over the fleet's backstage bases in their single-slash URL form), the app-config and values ConfigMaps, the Secrets the chart reads its credentials from, the plugin signing keys, the tunnel's SPIFFE bundle reference — and, on an installation without the agent platform, the portal's Dex client in the installation's dex-app configmap patch. A key an installation carries that no input renders and that removals.yaml does not list refuses the render, naming the key. Annotations: x-source says where a value comes from (registry: read from the installations registry, never typed; person: typed by the person enabling or reconciling; generated: created by the engine once and read back from the checkout afterwards). x-feature names the consistency feature of features.yaml the input's dimensions roll up to. x-files names the repository file a fileset key is read back from (<name> the installation; document the path in the file the keys are read under: the app-config is YAML text in its ConfigMap); x-readback on a person input names the file and key its value is read back from on record, and lays the value over the record; on a registry input it names where the record carries the fact, answered next to it and never laid over — the fact on record stands (key one path, or a list of paths the record may carry the value under, the first on record answering; kind value, present, host, installation — the installation whose base domain the URL's host is once prefix, its service label, is stripped — or file — whether the file is on record; prefix what the value carries in the file, stripped; a step of the key into a list is its index or a [key=value] selector, the entry whose key has the value; into YAML text what it decodes to). x-renders lists the key paths the input produces, prefixed by the file: backstage:kustomization (extras/backstage/kustomization.yaml and extras/backstage/backstage/kustomization.yaml), backstage:app-config (the app-config ConfigMap's backstage.appConfig), backstage:user-values (the user-values ConfigMap), backstage:file (a file of the portal's directory), dex-configmap (the dex-app configmap patch). List indices are written [*], per-installation map keys <name>. A default is declared only where every portal agrees.

installation.description: Facts about the installation that are on record. Read from the installations registry; never typed.

name.description: The installation's codename: the portal's sign-in provider oidc-<name>, its Kubernetes cluster entry, its installation entry and the Dex client's environment variables AUTH_DEX_<NAME>_CLIENT_ID and _CLIENT_SECRET derive from it.

baseDomain.description: The installation's base domain; the Dex, API and reading hosts derive from it.

customer.description: The owning organisation as the management-clusters and configs repositories name it.

provider.description: The infrastructure provider, shown on the installation entry.

providers.description: The providers the installation's entry lists: its own and, where it runs clusters on another besides (capv next to capa), that one too. Its own provider alone when absent.

region.description: The installation's region, shown on the installation entry; a provider without regions (cloud-director) has none and the entry carries no region.

pipeline.description: The installation's release pipeline (stable, testing), shown on the installation entry.

agentPlatform.description: The agent-platform capability is enabled on this installation. Then the portal's extras/backstage/kustomization.yaml lists the agent-platform definition's Component (./agent-platform/), that definition owns the installation's dex-app configmap patch and carries the portal's Dex client in it, this definition renders no dex patch, and the user values carry the installation's avatars host (https://avatars.<baseDomain>) first in BACKSTAGE_AVATARS_IMG_SRC of backstage.extraEnvVars, the CSP image source the shared base's csp.imgSrc reads (its default is 'self'), followed space-separated by the avatars host of every federated installation that runs the platform (federation.installations[*].agentPlatform); the variable is not set where no installation the portal shows runs the platform. backstage.extraEnvVars is one list Helm replaces wholesale across the HelmRelease's values sources, so the user values own it whole and the Component sets none.

portal.description: The portal as the person names it.

domain.description: The portal's hostname: its route, its base URLs, CORS origin and the Dex client's redirect URI.

organization.description: The organisation's name as the portal shows it.

supportUrl.description: Where the home page's support link goes: the customer's support channel. Without it, no home page resources block. Read back from the resources entry with the support link's icon, LiveHelp.

telemetrydeckAppId.description: The TelemetryDeck app the portal reports usage to; the salt is generated. Without it, no telemetry block.

friendlyLabels.description: Labels the portal's cluster pages show under a friendly name: a selector (a label key, or a glob over keys) with the name shown, a colour variant and a map of shown values. Without it, no friendly labels.

friendlyAnnotations.description: Annotations the portal's cluster pages show under a friendly name, in the same form as friendlyLabels. Without it, no friendly annotations.

federation.description: A portal over several installations of one customer. Every installation listed is shown next to the portal's own — a Kubernetes cluster entry and an installation entry — and has a provider oidc-<name> on its Dex whose client credentials are supplied at commit (federation.<name>.clientId and clientSecret, into user-secrets-backstage under dexAuthCredentials.<name>). signInInstallation names the installation whose Dex signs people in to the portal, the portal's own when absent. tokenBroker names the installation whose muster brokers cluster tokens for the others: then the portal has the sign-in installation's provider alone, the broker's client credentials are supplied at commit (federation.tokenBroker.clientId and clientSecret, dexAuthCredentials.musterBroker) and every installation other than the broker's carries clusterTokenAudience. Without a federation, the portal shows its own installation alone; a federation naming the sign-in installation alone, as the record reads back, is the portal's own installation signing in.

installations.description: The other installations the portal shows, with their facts on record, whether each runs the agent platform among them. Derived from the portal's gs.installations on record — every entry but the host, by name — and never typed outside a dry run; an entry the installations registry does not know refuses the comparison naming it.

name.description: The installation's codename: its provider oidc-<name>, its cluster entry, its installation entry and its credentials' environment variables derive from it.

baseDomain.description: The installation's base domain; its Dex and API hosts derive from it.

providers.description: The providers the installation's entry lists.

region.description: The installation's region; a provider without regions has none.

agentPlatform.description: The agent-platform capability is enabled on this installation: the portal shows its agents, so the user values list its avatars host (https://avatars.<baseDomain>) in BACKSTAGE_AVATARS_IMG_SRC of backstage.extraEnvVars, the CSP image source the shared base's csp.imgSrc reads, space-separated after the portal's own installation's host where that runs the platform, the federated installations in list order; without it the browser blocks the avatar images the installation's platform serves. The variable is not set where no installation the portal shows runs the platform and the shared base's 'self' stands.

private.description: The portal reaches the installation's API through the hub's tunnel: the installation is private and its cluster entry is the tunnel Service on the hub, https://kubernetes-<name>.agent-platform.svc.cluster.local:8443 with skipTLSVerify (the Service presents a SPIFFE certificate), instead of its public API. Read from the record: the entry's cluster URL is the tunnel Service's. Never typed outside a dry run.

signInInstallation.description: The installation whose Dex signs people in to the portal: its own or one it federates. Read back from gs.authProvider, its oidc- prefix stripped.

tokenBroker.description: The installation whose muster brokers cluster tokens for the others: its own or one it federates. Read back as the installation whose muster the broker's token URL names: the URL's host without its muster label is the installation's base domain.

line.description: The semver range the portal's OCIRepository follows, patched over the fleet base's tag.

plugins.description: The portal's plugins beyond the always-on techdocs, kubernetes, permission and catalog.

github.description: The GitHub integration through a GitHub App. Its app id, client id, client secret, private key and webhook secret are supplied at commit (plugins.github.appId, clientId, clientSecret, privateKey, webhookSecret) and land in the Secret github-app-credentials-backstage, which the chart writes into github-app-credentials.yaml.

enabled.description: Render the integration, its Secret and the Secret's values source.

appId.description: The GitHub App's id — an identifier, not a credential, but it lives only in the Secret's encrypted values: not read back, never set in the document, supplied at commit as plugins.github.appId like the credentials.

grafana.description: The Grafana plugin (@backstage-community/plugin-grafana). Its section is always rendered — the plugin's config schema requires it, and a portal without it does not start — with one host: the installation's own Grafana, https://grafana.<installation base domain>, under the installation's name. enabled says whether the plugin is wired: the dashboards card reads Grafana's search API through the portal's proxy at /grafana/api, whose service-account token is supplied at commit (plugins.grafana.token) and lands in user-secrets-backstage as grafana.apiToken, the value the chart exposes as GRAFANA_TOKEN; and the card, disabled in the app until a portal opts in, is switched on through the extension list the app-config includes.

enabled.description: Whether the plugin is wired: on, the proxy entry /grafana/api against the installation's Grafana, its token from the Secret, and the dashboards card switched on — app.extensions includes the shared list with the card (shared-config.yaml#extensionsGrafanaDashboards; the agent-platform Component's fragment includes its own pair with the platform's section, since Backstage keeps the later file's list whole); off, the section alone and the baseline list. Read back from the proxy entry's presence; the list follows it, never a choice.

domain.description: The installation's own Grafana: https://grafana.<installation base domain>, the one host of grafana.hosts and, wired, the proxy's target. Derived from the installation's base domain, never typed. Read back from the first host, else from grafana.domain, the plugin's deprecated single-host form, so the Grafana a portal names on record shows next to the installation's; a portal that names another one is off the definition at the host.

gitRepositoryPatterns.description: How a GitRepository's URL maps to a browsable file URL, for hosts the plugin does not know.

targetUrl.description: The file URL template over the pattern's named groups.

gitRepositoryUrlPattern.description: The regular expression with named groups the repository URL matches.

sentry.description: Error reporting to Sentry. The DSNs of the app and the backend and the CSP report URI are supplied at commit as they are (plugins.sentry.appDsn, backendDsn, reportUri: the DSN and the URI, never their base64) and land in user-secrets-backstage as their base64: the backstage chart copies sentry.app.dsn, sentry.backend.dsn and sentry.reportURI under its Secret's data: as they are and the pod loads that Secret with envFrom, so the render encodes them.

enabled.description: Render the error reporters, the CSP report URI and the Secret's sentry values.

tunnel.description: The tunnel to another installation's agent platform through tunnelport.

enabled.description: Render the tunnel's SPIFFE trust bundle reference: the ExternalSecret that copies the bundle from the platform namespace into the portal's, with its store and reader, the volume and mount that put it under /app/tunnelport-spiffe-bundle in the portal's container, and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS on its svid_bundle.pem in backstage.extraEnvVars of the user values — the one variable Node reads extra CA certificates through, so the backend trusts the SVIDs the tunnel Services present; without it the mount is inert.

pluginKeys.description: The portal's generated credentials: the plugin-to-plugin signing key pair (Secret plugin-keys-backstage, mounted by the chart under /app/plugin-keys/<keyId>/ and read by backend.auth.pluginKeyStore), the session secret and the Dex client secret (Secret user-secrets-backstage; the client secret is the same value as in the Dex client's Secret dex-client-backstage) and the telemetry salt. The engine creates them once and reads them back from the checkout afterwards; no person value.

keyId.description: The signing key pair's id, the directory the chart mounts it under.

selector.description: The label or annotation key, or a glob over keys.

key.description: The name shown in place of the key.

variant.description: The colour variant of the chip.

valueMap.description: The value shown per raw value.
